blocks.zh: 玻璃容器定義與分類
blocks.en: Definition and Classification of Glass Containers

blocks.zh: 兩種基礎玻璃材質
blocks.en: The Two Basic Glass Materials

blocks.zh: 三種型別分類（依耐水解性）
blocks.en: Three Types (Classified by Hydrolytic Resistance)

blocks.zh: 耐水解性的量測方法
blocks.en: How Hydrolytic Resistance Is Measured

blocks.zh: 「耐水解性」不是抽象概念——Ph.Eur. 用滴定法量化：將水與玻璃接觸後，量測釋出的鹼性離子（以0.01 M或0.02 M鹽酸反滴定），單位為mL HCl/100 mL溶液（Test A）或mL HCl/g玻璃（Test B）。數值越小，耐水解性越好。
blocks.en: "Hydrolytic resistance" is not an abstract concept. Ph.Eur. quantifies it by titration: water is brought into contact with the glass, and the alkali ions released are measured (back-titrated with 0.01 M or 0.02 M hydrochloric acid). The result is expressed in mL HCl/100 mL solution (Test A) or mL HCl/g glass (Test B). The lower the value, the better the hydrolytic resistance.

blocks.zh: 各型別適用製劑建議
blocks.en: Recommended Preparations for Each Type

blocks.zh: 選用決策矩陣
blocks.en: Selection Decision Matrix

blocks.zh: 「更高型別亦可用」原則
blocks.en: The "Higher Type May Also Be Used" Principle

blocks.zh: 如同選購材料規格「向上相容」：Type I的耐水解性高於Type II和III，因此若建議最低為Type II，使用Type I也合規。但不可反向替換——不能用Type III代替應使用Type II的場合。
blocks.en: Think of it as "upward compatibility" in a material specification: Type I has higher hydrolytic resistance than Type II and Type III, so if Type II is the recommended minimum, using Type I is also compliant. The reverse does not hold: Type III cannot replace Type II where Type II should be used.

blocks.zh: CDMO重要法規要求
blocks.en: Key Regulatory Requirements for CDMOs

blocks.zh: 不得重複使用：除Type I外，所有型別的玻璃容器不可重複用於藥品生產；輸血袋/血液製品容器一律不得重複使用。
blocks.en: No reuse: apart from Type I, glass containers of all types must not be reused for pharmaceutical production; containers for transfusion bags/blood products must never be reused.

blocks.zh: 感光產品：需使用有色玻璃（棕色/琥珀色），並符合光譜透射率限度（Test C，見Section 3）。
blocks.en: Light-sensitive products: coloured glass (brown/amber) must be used and must meet the spectral transmission limits (Test C, see Section 3).

blocks.zh: 視覺可檢查性：液體注射劑和注射用粉末的容器應允許可見異物目視檢查（即需有足夠透明度）。
blocks.en: Visual inspectability: containers for liquid injections and powders for injection should allow visual inspection for visible particles (that is, they need sufficient transparency).

blocks.zh: 內表面處理：Type II的高耐水解性依賴內表面處理（硫磺化處理），若此表面被破壞（如高溫滅菌過度），耐性會降低。
blocks.en: Internal surface treatment: the high hydrolytic resistance of Type II depends on an internal surface treatment (sulfur treatment). If this surface is damaged (for example by excessive high-temperature sterilization), the resistance falls.

blocks.zh: 生產要求 — 玻璃脫層（Delamination）
blocks.en: Production Requirements: Glass Delamination

blocks.zh: 玻璃脫層：重要安全風險
blocks.en: Glass Delamination: A Major Safety Risk

blocks.zh: 脫層（Delamination）是玻璃內表面剝落成薄片（lamellae/flakes）的現象，是注射劑中可見異物和次可見微粒的重要來源之一。FDA於2011年曾發出多起因玻璃脫層造成的藥品召回（recall），引發業界高度重視。
blocks.en: Delamination is the flaking of the glass inner surface into thin lamellae/flakes. It is one of the major sources of visible and subvisible particles in injectables. In 2011 the FDA issued a number of drug recalls caused by glass delamination, which drew strong attention from industry.

blocks.zh: 脫層高風險因素
blocks.en: High-Risk Factors for Delamination

blocks.zh: 緩衝劑：檸檬酸鹽（citrate）和磷酸鹽（phosphate）緩衝液對玻璃腐蝕性強，顯著增加脫層風險。
blocks.en: Buffers: citrate and phosphate buffers are highly corrosive to glass and markedly increase the risk of delamination.

blocks.zh: 高離子強度：高鹽製劑加速玻璃表面侵蝕。
blocks.en: High ionic strength: high-salt formulations accelerate attack on the glass surface.

blocks.zh: 終端滅菌（Terminal sterilization）：高溫（121°C）蒸汽滅菌會促進玻璃-藥液反應，增加脫層風險。
blocks.en: Terminal sterilization: high-temperature (121°C) steam sterilization promotes glass-solution reactions and increases the risk of delamination.

blocks.zh: 玻璃管製造工藝：玻璃管成型時的溫度-時間曲線影響內表面結構。
blocks.en: Glass tube manufacturing process: the temperature-time profile during tube forming affects the structure of the inner surface.

blocks.zh: 延遲顯現：脫層通常在充填後數月才肉眼可見——IPC檢查時可能不被發現。
blocks.en: Delayed onset: delamination usually becomes visible to the naked eye only months after filling, so it may not be detected at IPC inspection.

blocks.zh: 脫層傾向評估方法
blocks.en: Methods for Assessing Delamination Propensity

blocks.zh: 加速降解試驗（Accelerated degradation testing）：在規定溫度下短時間暴露，以實際製劑溶液為萃取液，檢測：粒子出現、內表面相分離、矽濃度急劇升高。
blocks.en: Accelerated degradation testing: short exposure at a defined temperature, using the actual drug product solution as the extraction medium, to detect: appearance of particles, phase separation of the inner surface, and a sharp rise in silicon concentration.

blocks.zh: 正式相容性穩定性測試：加速試驗只作為篩選工具（預測性），最終需在正常條件下進行完整穩定性試驗確認玻璃與藥液的相容性。
blocks.en: Formal compatibility stability testing: accelerated testing is only a (predictive) screening tool. A full stability study under normal conditions is ultimately needed to confirm the compatibility of the glass with the drug solution.

blocks.zh: CDMO應對措施
blocks.en: CDMO Actions

blocks.zh: 新產品容器選型時進行玻璃相容性研究，特別是pH >7或含磷酸鹽/檸檬酸鹽緩衝液的製劑。
blocks.en: Conduct a glass compatibility study when selecting containers for new products, especially for formulations with pH >7 or containing phosphate/citrate buffers.

blocks.zh: 終端滅菌產品：評估玻璃脫層風險，考慮優先選用Type I（耐性最高）。
blocks.en: Terminally sterilized products: assess the risk of glass delamination and consider giving preference to Type I (highest resistance).

blocks.zh: 參考USP <1660>（Evaluation of the Inner Surface Durability of Glass Containers）和PDA TR87中的相容性評估框架。
blocks.en: Refer to the compatibility assessment frameworks in USP <1660> (Evaluation of the Inner Surface Durability of Glass Containers) and PDA TR87.

blocks.zh: 試驗概覽與耐水解性試驗選用
blocks.en: Test Overview and Selection of Hydrolytic Resistance Tests

blocks.zh: 耐水解性三種試驗及用途
blocks.en: The Three Hydrolytic Resistance Tests and Their Uses

blocks.zh: Test A + B（或A + C）組合邏輯
blocks.en: Logic of the Test A + B (or A + C) Combination

blocks.zh: Test A區分「高耐水解性（Type I或II）vs 中等耐水解性（Type III）」，但無法區分Type I與Type II——因為兩者Test A結果可能相近（都高）。需要Test B（玻璃本身組成試驗）或Test C（蝕刻後看內表面是否受損）才能進一步區分：若Test A後蝕刻（Test C）大幅升高→有表面處理→Type II；若不變→Type I。
blocks.en: Test A distinguishes "high hydrolytic resistance (Type I or II)" from "moderate hydrolytic resistance (Type III)", but cannot tell Type I from Type II, because their Test A results can be similar (both high). Test B (composition of the glass itself) or Test C (checking after etching whether the inner surface is damaged) is needed to separate them further: if the result after etching (Test C) rises substantially, a surface treatment is present and the container is Type II; if it is unchanged, the container is Type I.

blocks.zh: 額外必做試驗
blocks.en: Additional Mandatory Tests

blocks.zh: 砷（Arsenic）試驗：適用於水性注射劑用Type I和II玻璃容器。限度：≤ 0.1 ppm As（氫化物生成AAS法，193.7 nm）。
blocks.en: Arsenic test: applies to Type I and II glass containers for aqueous injections. Limit: ≤ 0.1 ppm As (hydride generation AAS method, 193.7 nm).

blocks.zh: 光譜透射率：適用於有色玻璃容器。UV-Vis測量290–450 nm範圍（見Section 3表3.2.1-5）。
blocks.en: Spectral transmission: applies to coloured glass containers. UV-Vis measurement over the 290–450 nm range (see Table 3.2.1-5 in Section 3).

blocks.zh: 玻璃器皿預處理要求
blocks.en: Glassware Pretreatment Requirements

blocks.zh: 用於試驗的燒瓶和燒杯需已使用過，或已在121°C高壓滅菌≥1小時——目的是將器皿的可浸出物先行飽和，避免干擾樣品的滴定結果（空白值偏高）。這是精準滴定試驗的前處理控制措施。
blocks.en: The flasks and beakers used for the tests must have been used before, or have been autoclaved at 121°C for ≥1 hour. The purpose is to saturate the leachables of the glassware beforehand so that they do not interfere with the sample titration (high blank values). This is a pretreatment control for accurate titration testing.

blocks.zh: 充填容積（Filling Volume）測定
blocks.en: Determination of Filling Volume

blocks.zh: 充填容積的定義和計算
blocks.en: Definition and Calculation of Filling Volume

blocks.zh: 充填容積是試驗中注入水的體積——代表「實際使用狀態下的液體量」。規定如下：
blocks.en: The filling volume is the volume of water introduced in the test, representing "the volume of liquid in actual use". It is specified as follows:

blocks.zh:
小瓶/瓶：Filling volume = 滿裝容積（brimful capacity） × 0.9
安瓿：Filling volume = 充填至「肩部起始點（point A）」的體積
注射器/卡匣：Filling volume = 滿裝容積 × 0.9
blocks.en:
Vials/bottles: Filling volume = brimful capacity × 0.9
Ampoules: Filling volume = volume filled up to the "start of the shoulder (point A)"
Syringes/cartridges: Filling volume = brimful capacity × 0.9

blocks.zh: 採用90%而非100%的原因：模擬實際使用時的充填狀態（通常不充填至溢出），同時確保蒸壓時液體不溢出。
blocks.en: Why 90% rather than 100%: to simulate the filling state in actual use (containers are normally not filled to overflowing), and to ensure the liquid does not overflow during autoclaving.

blocks.zh: 充填容積的重要性
blocks.en: Why Filling Volume Matters

blocks.zh: 充填容積直接決定Test A的試驗液體積（Table 3.2.1-2，見Section 2）和所需的滴定次數。充填容積越大，接觸面積越大，萃取的鹼性離子越多，但稀釋體積也更大。正確測定充填容積是確保試驗結果可重現的前提。
blocks.en: The filling volume directly determines the volume of test solution for Test A (Table 3.2.1-2, see Section 2) and the number of titrations required. The larger the filling volume, the larger the contact area and the more alkali ions are extracted, but the dilution volume is also larger. Determining the filling volume correctly is a prerequisite for reproducible test results.

blocks.zh: 安瓿的「肩部（Shoulder）」
blocks.en: The "Shoulder" of an Ampoule

blocks.zh: 安瓿的充填容積特別規定至「肩部」，即玻璃體開始收縮變細之處（Figure 3.2.1-1所示的point A）。這是因為安瓿的頸部較窄，充填至頸部會影響試驗操作；填至肩部是最能代表實際藥液充填量的位置。
blocks.en: The filling volume of an ampoule is specified specifically up to the "shoulder", the point where the glass body begins to taper (point A shown in Figure 3.2.1-1). This is because the neck of an ampoule is narrow, and filling to the neck would interfere with the test procedure; the shoulder is the position that best represents the actual fill volume of the drug solution.

blocks.zh: 6個容器取樣的統計意義
blocks.en: Statistical Meaning of Sampling Six Containers

blocks.zh: 選取6個容器（大容量≥100 mL選3個），計算平均充填容積——這是為了考慮同一批次容器的容積均勻性。若單取1個容器可能因製造偏差而不具代表性，6個平均值能更準確反映批次實際充填容積。
blocks.en: Six containers are selected (three for large-volume containers of ≥100 mL) and the mean filling volume is calculated, to account for the volume uniformity within a batch of containers. A single container may not be representative because of manufacturing variation; the mean of six reflects the actual filling volume of the batch more accurately.
